topics.name: Kinds of sentences (assertive, interrogative, imperative, exclamatory)
Opposites with prefixes (un-, im-, in-, dis-, ir-)

questions.rule: Use How + adjective in this exclamation (What needs a noun), and plural flowers takes are.

options: It is impossible to lift this heavy pot alone.
It is unpossible to lift this heavy pot alone.
It is dispossible to lift this heavy pot alone.
questions.rule: The opposite of possible is made with im-: impossible.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: Revathi found that someone has moved the pot.
Revathi found that someone had moved the pot.
Revathi found that someone had move the pot.
questions.rule: The moving happened before she found it, so use the past perfect: had moved.

options: She hardly had no time to practise.
She didn't hardly have any time to practise.
She hardly had any time to practise.
questions.rule: Hardly is already negative, so don't add no or not: hardly had any time.

options: Please don't play that quick tune.
Please don't plays that quick tune.
Please not play that quick tune.
questions.rule: A negative command uses Don't + the base verb: don't play.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct question tag.
options: The organisers were not convinced, weren't they?
The organisers were not convinced, were they?
The organisers were not convinced, did they?
questions.rule: A negative sentence takes a positive tag with the same helper: were not ... were they?

options: Neither the pot nor the plants were in the courtyard.
Neither the pot nor the plants was in the courtyard.
Neither the pot or the plants were in the courtyard.
questions.rule: Neither pairs with nor, and the verb agrees with the nearer subject: the plants were.

options: By the time the contest began, a neighbour has already taken the pot to her house.
By the time the contest began, a neighbour had already taken the pot to her house.
By the time the contest began, a neighbour had already took the pot to her house.
questions.rule: The earlier past action takes had + past participle: had already taken.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Before the noun day we need an adjective, not an adverb: an unhappy day.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: In this exclamation Revathi is a singular subject, so the verb needs -s: Revathi plays.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The pot vanished before she reached the courtyard yesterday, so use had already vanished.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: No one is singular and the time is past: No one ... was.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Plays is simple present with she, so the tag uses does: doesn't she?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The past perfect is had + past participle: had never heard.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: How here describes the action carried, so it needs an adverb: How proudly ...!

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: With neither ... nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject: her two friends know.

questions.after: that the plants leaned towards the violin.
questions.rule: After It was we need an adjective: It was unusual that ...

questions.after: a surprise it was to see the plants move!
questions.rule: Use What a + noun in an exclamation: What a surprise ...!
The stealing happened before she was sad, so use the past perfect: had stolen.
Hardly is negative by itself, so it goes with any: hardly any.

questions.before: Revathi didn't tell anyone about her secret,
questions.rule: A negative past sentence takes a positive tag: didn't tell ... did she?

questions.prompt: Fill in the gap to make a command.
questions.rule: A negative imperative starts with Don't + base verb.

questions.after: from the courtyard before Revathi woke up.
questions.rule: The pot did not take anything; it was taken earlier: past perfect passive had been taken.

questions.before: No other balsam plant in the colony was as tall
questions.rule: The pattern is as tall as; than goes only with comparatives like taller.
Exclamation pattern: What a + adjective + noun + subject + verb + !
Subject + were unable to + base verb: Her friends were unable to find the pot.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence with a question tag.
questions.rule: A positive simple present sentence takes doesn't she?
The earlier action (had flowered) comes in the past perfect; the later one (began) in the simple past.

questions.prompt: Make an affirmative sentence with 'failed to'.
questions.rule: Failed to + base verb gives a negative meaning without a negative word.

chat: Did you see Revathi's plants at the show?
questions.rule: After didn't, use the base verb: didn't see.

chat: Did the judges agree with Revathi at first?
questions.rule: The opposite of agree is made with dis-: disagreed.

chat: Why were you late for the plant show?
options: The bus had already left when I reached the stop.
The bus has already left when I reached the stop.
The bus had already leave when I reached the stop.
questions.rule: The bus left before you reached: had already left.

chat: You're coming to the prize distribution, aren't you?
options: Yes, I am. You'll come too, won't you?
Yes, I am. You'll come too, aren't you?
Yes, I am. You'll come too, don't you?
questions.rule: A positive sentence with will takes a negative tag: won't you?

chat: Give me an example of an imperative sentence.
questions.rule: An imperative uses the base verb: Please water the plants.

chat: Was there any breeze yesterday evening?
options: No, there was hardly no breeze.
No, there was hardly any breeze.
No, there were hardly any breeze.
questions.rule: Hardly needs any, and uncountable breeze takes was.

chat: Why didn't the organisers believe me at first?
options: Because they had never seen plants respond to music before.
Because they had never see plants respond to music before.
Because they had never seen plants responds to music before.
questions.rule: Past perfect = had + past participle (seen); after seen plants use the base verb respond.

chat: Revathi won the first prize for her plants!
options: What a wonderful news that is!
questions.rule: News is uncountable and singular: no a, and it takes is.

questions.source: There are a few benches in the park.
options: There are not few benches in the park.
There are not many benches in the park.
There is not many benches in the park.
questions.rule: A few = not many; plural benches keeps are.

options: How bright were the flowers were!
questions.rule: Drop very, start with How + adjective, then subject + verb in the same tense: How bright the flowers were!

questions.source: The noise did not disturb Revathi.
options: The noise failed to disturb Revathi.
The noise failed to disturbed Revathi.
The noise fails to disturb Revathi.
questions.rule: Did not disturb = failed to disturb: past tense kept, base verb after to.

questions.source: What a sweet tune Revathi played!
options: Revathi plays a very sweet tune.
Revathi played a very sweet tunes.
Revathi played a very sweet tune.
questions.rule: What a sweet tune becomes a very sweet tune; the tense stays past: played.

questions.source: Revathi's plants were healthier than the other plants.
options: The other plants were not as healthier as Revathi's plants.
The other plants were not as healthy as Revathi's plants.
Revathi's plants were not as healthy as the other plants.
questions.rule: Swap the subjects and use the plain adjective: The other plants were not as healthy as ...

questions.source: Revathi watered the plants. Then she played her violin.
options: After Revathi has watered the plants, she played her violin.
After Revathi had water the plants, she played her violin.
After Revathi had watered the plants, she played her violin.
questions.rule: The first action takes the past perfect: After Revathi had watered ..., she played ...

questions.source: Her mother said that she knew nothing about the pot.
options: Her mother denied to know anything about the pot.
Her mother denied knowing anything about the pot.
Her mother denied knowing nothing about the pot.
questions.rule: Deny is followed by an -ing form, and nothing becomes anything.

questions.prompt: Change into an interrogative sentence without changing the meaning.
questions.rule: Everyone loves becomes the question Who does not love ...?; after does use the base verb.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Had been + past participle: had been taken. Refused to + base verb: refused to give.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Plural flowers look. They are takes the tag aren't they?

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Refused to and failed to are followed by the base verb: listen, stop.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Had been taken (past perfect passive); arrived matches saw; How shocked she was!

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: After Do use the base verb have; the past of bend is bent; every organiser is singular: was.
